title: Following Pointer Chains
summary: Real programs reach data through several levels of pointers - a game reaches a player's health through the world, the level and the player. A chain can be written as a base address and a list of offsets, followed one read at a time with a null check at every step. Why chains survive restarts when single addresses do not.

cards.q: In the chain base -> 0x00 -> 0x00 -> 0x08 -> 0x10 -> 0x04, why is the last offset added without a read?
cards.a: The last step gives the address of the value itself; every earlier step reads a pointer to the next object.

cards.q: Why must a chain be checked for nullptr at every step?
cards.a: Any object along the path may not exist at that moment; reading through its null pointer would crash.

cards.q: Why does the address of health change between runs while the chain stays the same?
cards.a: Heap allocations and the program's load address change every run, but the struct offsets are compiled in and the first link is anchored to a global at a fixed offset inside the program.

cards.q: Where does offset 0x08 in the World step come from?
cards.a: From the struct layout: offsetof(World, players), after the int tick and 4 bytes of padding.
